source: YouTube search (Shorts by relevance and by views, long-form by views and by views this year) across 6 niches, about 1,600 videos; opening lines read from captions of the top 77. Views as of 2026-11-27. Openings are trimmed to the first line.
what_the_top_openings_share: The first spoken line is the title, nearly word for word (Yee Yee Life, Tyler Vitelli, Isaiah Photo, Hormozi).
A number is in the first five words: a time, a price, a weight or a count.
The bar to clear is stated before the attempt, often with why it is hard ("less than 1% of people can").
Escalation formats say the ladder up front ("higher and higher, all the way up to a .50 cal"), so the end is promised.
Teaching clips that did best open on the wrong way first ("this is not how you grip a pistol").
Gym humour skits are the biggest bucket in powerlifting search and most have no voiceover: the caption sets the scene.
Lifters attempting a running bar (Larry Wheels 40 yd dash, Hamish James 5K, CBum sprinting) is a proven lane and it is Michael's.
Mocking the hybrid athlete already works (Hamish James 'How To Be A HYBRID ATHLETE', 2.0M).

challenge.name: Can I…?
challenge.why: A bar the viewer can picture (a time, a weight, a count) and one attempt to clear it. The question is open until the last second, so people stay for the result.
challenge.opening: Say the bar in the first sentence, with the number, and why it is hard ("less than 1% can"). Frame 1 is you at the start line or under the bar.
